claims.text: Introducing a surface coating can improve the high-temperature oxygen resistance of refractory high-entropy alloys.
Alloying with protective oxide-forming elements can improve the high-temperature oxygen resistance of refractory high-entropy alloys.
The proposed starting materials are as-cast or wrought refractory high-entropy alloys.
The intervention is either surface coating or alloying with protective oxide-forming elements.
The intervention will cause formation of a protective oxide layer.
The protective oxide layer prevents oxygen diffusion into the alloy.
Preventing oxygen diffusion into the alloy reduces oxidation.
The cited record node::W4306403397 provides transferable support for the proposed protective-oxide mechanism.
The treated alloy will have improved high-temperature oxygen resistance relative to an untreated refractory high-entropy alloy.
The treated alloy will exhibit reduced oxidation relative to the untreated alloy.
The proposed effect is expected between 800 and 1200 degrees Celsius in an oxidizing atmosphere.
Oxidation rate and microstructure will be measured during a high-temperature oxidation test.
The hypothesis will be falsified if the coated or alloyed alloys show no improvement in high-temperature oxygen resistance.
